mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain far below baseline while RETAIL_REC is also depressed, a continued low-commuting state will keep weekday foot traffic weak and push retail-and-recreation mobility slightly lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay near their current depressed levels for at least three of the four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and drifts upward while WORKPLACES remains weak, more people will substitute local discretionary trips for commuting, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL is at or above +5 and WORKPLACES stays below -30 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and WORKPLACES remains below -30 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in PARKS mobility below the recent +10 range will signal less outdoor leisure circulation, and that lost foot traffic will spill into weaker retail-and-recreation mobility over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below +8 after holding at or above +10 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days of a drop in PARKS below +8 from a prior-week level at or above +10.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve at the same time, the city is likely in a reopening or normalization phase that raises mixed-purpose trips and then lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by 5 points and WORKPLACES rises by 5 points within the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite simultaneous week-over-week gains of at least 5 points in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in GROCERY_PHARM together with weak TRANSIT indicates fewer routine out-of-home errands, which will suppress adjacent discretionary shopping and keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher than its last-four-week mean over the next 14 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT stay below their recent levels.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS keeps rising while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, warm-weather local recreation will substitute for indoor retail visits and reduce RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds +10 for two consecutive weeks and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above +10 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above +5 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in GROCERY_PHARM will first raise neighborhood trip density, then spill over into nearby retail and recreation spending, producing a higher RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 7 days after a week-over-week gain of at least 3 points in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays mildly elevated, the city is likely still under movement restraint, and that regime will keep retail-and-recreation mobility below the prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-four-week average over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -25 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5.
